findings.claim: CONFIRMED: `_whole_string` widens both name tiers to case-insensitive, but the `index` and `near` branches return before the uniqueness/ambiguity check, so a page carrying case-twin controls now silently resolves to a DIFFERENT element than before this PR — no `ambiguous-match`, no `narrowed:` note, and the docstring/ADR-026 claim that case twins 'collide as an ambiguity and go to M38's narrowing rungs' is false on those two paths.
findings.evidence:
resolver.py:334,337 (`_whole_string`) feeding :412-415 (`if index is not None: ... return loc.nth(index)`) and :397-405 (`near` returns `loc.nth(i)`), both BEFORE the `n == 1` check at :416 and the `ambiguous` bookkeeping at :418-419. Input 1 (index): `ADD TO CART` before `Add to cart`, target `{'role':'link','name':'Add to cart','index':0}`, action `click` — base 6b016b5 returns id=rowcta, HEAD returns id=promo, tier=role, narrowed=None. Input 2 (near): `SAVE FOR LATER` inside the row holding anchor 'Widget A', `Save for later` elsewhere, target `{'role':'link','name':'Save for later','near':'Widget A'}` — base returns id=real, HEAD returns id=twin, tier=structural, narrowed=None. `extract_all` grows the same way (`{'text':'Great'}` over `

Great

`/`

GREAT

`: base ['p1'], HEAD ['p1','p2']). No adversarial case in the diff covers this direction.
findings.repro: git worktree add /tmp/base 6b016b5 --detach; then call resolve({'role':'link','name':'Add to cart','index':0}, action='click') against both trees on a page with `ADD TO CART` before `Add to cart` — base returns rowcta, HEAD returns promo. Full script in the round-1 review relay.
findings.acceptance: A new adversarial case (watched red on `fbe304b`) that puts two case-twin controls on one fixture and asserts that an `index`/`near` target either raises `ambiguous-match` or records a narrowing label — plus either a code guard that runs the uniqueness/ambiguity check before `index`/`near` select, or the `_whole_string` docstring, ADR-026 and browser-domain/SKILL.md corrected to say the collision promise holds only on the `n == 1` path.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: `select_option` matches the requested string against `[value, label]` by list membership, so a value string that happens to equal a DIFFERENT option's value is selected, and an absent/empty `value` matches an empty-valued placeholder — both record `postcondition_ok: True` and report `success`.
findings.evidence: agent.py:1130 `match = next((o for o in opts if want in o), None)` with readback at :1138 comparing to `match[0]` (self-consistent by construction). Executed: on `<option value=''>Choose a filing…</option><option value='2024'>FY 2023</option><option value='2025'>FY 2024</option>`, `want='2024'` -> matched `['2024','FY 2023']`, selected value `'2024'`, postcondition_ok=True, page fires change to the FY 2023 filing. `want=''` (step omits `value`; :1100 `step.get('value') or ''`) -> matched `['','Choose a filing…']`, postcondition_ok=True — a filter never applied, recorded as applied. `press` refuses the same shape at :1145-1146; `select_option` does not, and nothing in `plan_gap`/:1002-1015 type-checks or requires the value. `loop-lab.html:11` ships exactly the `<option value=''>` placeholder shape. PRE-EXISTING: shipped with M42's select_option, not introduced by this PR.
findings.repro: Resolve the combobox, evaluate OPTIONS_JS, then `next((o for o in opts if want in o), None)` for want='2024' and want='' — both return a match whose readback passes.
findings.acceptance: Two adversarial cases, both watched red first: (i) a `<select>` whose option values collide with another option's label, asserting the step either selects the intended option or fails loudly rather than reporting success; (ii) a `select_option` step with no `value`, asserting a `task`-class refusal in the shape `press` already uses. Alternatively a declared limitation in docs/support-matrix.md naming both shapes.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: the new `resolve_advertised` check records only whether `resolve` RAISED, never whether it landed on the element the name was advertised for — so the round trip the case exists to close grades green when the observation's name resolves onto a different element.
findings.evidence: eval_adapter.py:2075-2089 — the loop calls `await resolve(page, target)` inside `try/except` and discards the returned locator; `passed` at :2122 only reads `not unresolvable`. Executed: a host page with `<button id=HOST-BTN>Continue</button>` and an iframe containing `<button id=INNER-BTN>Continue</button>` — `observe()` advertises TWO `{'role':'button','name':'Continue'}` entries (one per frame), and `resolve` returns `id=HOST-BTN` for BOTH because resolver.py:318 puts the main frame first; grader output `advertised_name_did_not_resolve = []`, `passed: True`. Same call site passes `task=''`/`action=''`, so `may_narrow` is False (resolver.py:324) — stricter than the executor for `extract` and still blind to identity. The new case names only 'combobox', so one element of the 60 in the observation is graded.
findings.repro: Build a host page with a same-named button in the main frame and in an iframe; loop observe()'s button entries through resolve() and print the resolved element id — both resolve to HOST-BTN while the grader reports passed.
findings.acceptance: `resolve_advertised` compares the resolved handle to the element the observation advertised (element handle identity, not just 'did not raise'), the check is exercised by a case that is red when a name round-trips onto the wrong element, and the `task`/`action` passed to `resolve` match what the executor would pass for that element's likely action.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: the two cases the new case's `note` names as the wait's ablations never enter the new branch, and the 'options never arrive' path — 10.0s per step with the TimeoutError swallowed — has no eval case at all.
findings.evidence: agent.py:1108-1129 (`if not opts:` ... `except Exception: pass`). Both named ablations, `action-select-option-refuses-an-absent-option.json` and `action-select-option-verifies-by-readback.json`, run against `loop-lab.html:10-14`, whose `<select id='fx'>` carries three in-document `<option>`s — so `opts` is non-empty and the branch is dead in both. Measured on a `<select>` that never fills: waited 10.0s, `swallowed: TimeoutError`, `opts=[]`. The new case only exercises the success side (options arrive at 1.0s). The commoner real shape — a placeholder `<option>` replaced by fetch — has `opts != []` and never enters the branch either.
findings.repro: Resolve a combobox on `<select id=f aria-label=Filing></select>` that never fills, run the branch's wait, and time it: 10.0s, TimeoutError swallowed, opts=[].
findings.acceptance: An adversarial case on a `<select>` whose options never arrive, watched red first, asserting the loud `act` failure AND bounding the wall clock it costs (or a shorter timeout justified against the `fast` band); plus the `note` in `action-select-option-waits-for-fetch-painted-options.json` corrected — the two cases it names are not ablations of this branch.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: the PR's own invariant — a name the observation advertises is a name `resolve` accepts — is enforced only for the `name`/`text` tiers; a `near` anchor quoted verbatim from the same observation is still matched case-sensitively at `_nearest`'s exact pass and degrades to the substring pass the docstring itself calls risky, with no narrowing label.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:265 `passes = [('exact', lambda: page.get_by_text(near, exact=True)), ('substring', lambda: page.get_by_text(near))]` — untouched by this PR. Executed on `<style>th{text-transform:uppercase}</style>` with rows `Total`/`10` and `Subtotal of Total line`/`99`: `observe()` advertises the anchor as 'TOTAL' (the only spelling a planner can quote), and `{'role':'cell','near':'TOTAL'}` raises `ResolveError: proximity to 'TOTAL' does not identify one element` because the exact pass finds 0 and the substring pass finds 2, while `{'role':'cell','near':'Total'}` — a string nothing in the observation contains — resolves cleanly to '10'. The new `resolve_advertised` key only feeds `{role, name}`, so no case covers the `near` half of the round trip.
findings.repro: On the uppercase-th table, resolve `{'role':'cell','near':'TOTAL'}` (the observed spelling) and `{'role':'cell','near':'Total'}` — the observed one raises, the unobservable one resolves.
findings.acceptance: Either `_nearest`'s exact pass uses the same whole-string case-insensitive matcher (with a case pinning it red first), or `resolve_advertised` is extended to feed advertised names back as `near` anchors and the residual asymmetry is declared in docs/support-matrix.md.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: `_whole_string` calls `.split()` unguarded, so a non-string `name`/`text` raises `AttributeError` before any Playwright call and the step's failure class regresses from `locate` to `act` — a graded output (INV-1 diagnosis accuracy).
findings.evidence: resolver.py:199 `r'\s+'.join(re.escape(w) for w in s.split())`, reached from :334/:337. Input `{'text': 4.82}` (a JSON number; agent.py:1002-1003 validates target KEYS only). Base 6b016b5: `ResolveError: no tier resolved {'text': 4.82}` -> `agent.classify` at agent.py:226-227 returns 'locate'. HEAD: `AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'split'` -> falls to agent.py:228 and is labelled 'act' for any non-navigate action. REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THIS PR.
findings.repro: Call resolve(page, {'text': 4.82}, action='extract') on both trees and pass the exception to agent.classify — base gives 'locate', HEAD gives 'act'.
findings.acceptance: An adversarial case with a non-string `name`/`text` target, watched red first, asserting failure class `locate` (or a `task`-class plan refusal in the shape `unsupported target key(s)` uses) — not `act`.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED (pre-existing, untouched, now inconsistent with the invariant this PR establishes): `check_state`'s `role_visible` postcondition uses `get_by_role(role, name=<str>)` with neither `exact` nor `_whole_string`, i.e. case-insensitive SUBSTRING, so a postcondition is satisfied by an element the plan did not name.
findings.evidence:
agent.py:526-527. Executed: on `

Shopping Cart is empty

`, `check_state(page, {'role_visible': {'role':'heading','name':'Cart'}})` returns True. The whole argument of resolver.py:325-330 — 'substring matching resolved absent targets to superstring siblings and extracted the wrong element as a success' — applies verbatim to a postcondition, which is what `verify` treats as proof the action landed.
findings.repro: check_state(pg, {'role_visible': {'role':'heading','name':'Cart'}}) on a page whose only heading reads 'Shopping Cart is empty' returns True.
findings.acceptance: Either `role_visible` uses `_whole_string` too, pinned by a case that is red on the 'Cart' vs 'Shopping Cart is empty' input, or a debt item naming the asymmetry so the next reader does not assume the matcher is shared.
